title: Facilitator in Microsoft Teams: what does the meeting agent do, and who can switch it off?
summary: Hold: the blocking command's cited reference describes its value as unblocking, and the retention command only creates a policy rather than setting retention. The availability-change timing also omits Microsoft's warning that changes can take six days in rare cases.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; What it is; What to check
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > actions menu > Allow or Block controls the app's allowed state.
claims.quote:
In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select Facilitator from the app list.
In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; writer evidence: blocks with IsBlocked $true
claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is the displayed blocking automation.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Replace the fixed-value call with 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked <boolean>' and add this note: 'The reference documents the Boolean state parameter but describes both $true and $false examples as unblocking; it does not reliably establish the blocking value. Use the documented admin UI to block Facilitator.' Do not claim that $true blocks it.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; What to check
claims.claim: Manage apps > Facilitator > Users and groups > Availability > Edit availability > Available to manages app availability.
claims.quote:
Select the Users and groups tab.
Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability.
Select Edit availability.
Select the required option from Available to menu.
claims.fix: Use 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to'. The already-cited Facilitator page supplies Teams apps > Manage apps and names the app.

claims.where: controls[6].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Purview > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies is the location for Facilitator retention policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies and create a retention policy
claims.fix: Keep the path and add to the row note: 'This opens the retention-policy list; create a retention policy using Teams chats for meeting interactions and OneDrive accounts for meeting notes.' The cited page stops at the list and links to policy creation.

claims.where: controls[6].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -TeamsChatLocation <locations> sets retention of Facilitator interactions and notes.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies).
claims.fix: Replace the API call with 'New-RetentionComplianceRule -Policy <policy name> -RetentionDuration <days> -RetentionComplianceAction <Keep, Delete or KeepAndDelete>' and its docs URL with https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule. Replace the last note sentence with 'Adds a retention rule to an existing policy already scoped to the appropriate Teams chats or OneDrive accounts location; duration is in days.' Add that reference to sources.

claims.where: controls[6].note; Governance controls table
